newsitem.title: NORWAY: Higher oil prices boost profits at Saga.
newsitem.headline: Higher oil prices boost profits at Saga.

text.p: Norway's largest private oil company Saga Petroleum ASA said on Thursday operating profits in the first eight months jumped 52 percent versus a year ago mainly due to higher oil prices and increased sales.
The group booked an operating result of 1.97 billion crowns ($302.3 million) versus 1.3 billion crowns in the corresponding 1995 period.

Pre-tax profits surged nearly 78 percent to 2.12 billion crowns against 1.2 billion crowns. The result included a gain of 171 million crowns from the sale of shares in Norwegian metal producer Elkem ASA, which was booked in the first four-month accounts.

Total oil sales to the end of August amounted to 28.9 million barrels, a rise of 14 percent from 25.3 million barrels a year ago. The average oil price was 127 crowns per barrel compared with 109 crowns in the 1995 period, Saga said.
Group oil inventories in the second tertial fell 1.7 million barrels to 0.2 million barrels, it said.

Production of crude, gas and natural gas liquids amounted to 4.7 million tonnes of oil equivalent, or 34.2 million barrels, of which 91 percent was oil. Output in the corresponding year-ago period was 30.2 million barrels. ($ = 6.517 Norwegian Crowns)
